title: I've been building a tower defense game with AI tools in my spare time. Here's what I've learned
author: TheBorzX
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/4fdyg4nycsdh1.png?width=960&format=png&auto=webp&s=96b07b419416dbe50183df5d7cd2c7cabb170caa

I've been working on a tower defense game called **Linegrid Siege TD** over the last few months, mostly in the evenings after work. I'm a Cloud Engineer during the day, so game development is just a hobby I really enjoy.

From the start, I wanted to see how much AI could actually help with making a game and not just writing code.

I've used AI for things like:

* Refactoring Flutter + Flame code
* Brainstorming gameplay ideas
* Creating and iterating on art assets
* Writing documentation and design docs
* Planning new features and balancing

What surprised me is that AI isn't the hard part. The hard part is still making thousands of small decisions, testing ideas, fixing bugs, and polishing everything until it feels right.

The biggest improvement for me came when I stopped asking random questions and started documenting the project properly. Once the AI had enough context, the quality of its suggestions improved a lot.

If anyone wants to see what all of this has turned into, here's the current build with a playble demo:

[https://ezhi-studio.itch.io/linegrid-siege-td](https://ezhi-studio.itch.io/linegrid-siege-td)

I'd really appreciate any feedback good or bad. I'm always looking for ways to improve it.

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body: Its a good start! Liked it. It has good onboading too. I would just make it less wordy, ppl do not like to read.

replies.author: TheBorzX
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback! 
I used to have less text to explain features, but feedback from people that never played a TD game couldn't fully understand the game UI and flow. So thats is why it is a lot of text at the moment.

comments.author: Kingnorik
comments.body:
The onboarding is too much. Maybe introduce features over the first wave. My only other critique is the selection. After placing a tower I would clear the selection. Currently you have to click the tower name again to deselect it before you can do anything else.

Overall I like it. Fun and I can see it will get hard and have good depth.

replies.author: TheBorzX
replies.body: Appreciate the feedback! I forgot to include an explanation of the mouse and keyboard shortcuts. Right-clicking cancels the currently selected building, so you can deselect it quickly. I'll definitely take another look at the onboarding process to make things clearer. Thanks for pointing it out!

comments.author: stickfigure
comments.body:
I really like the core gameplay loop! I also like the dynamic pathing - very well thought out, super fun! I got to level 3 and I'll play more again :)

Would love a campaign mode and I skipped on boarding 🔆

replies.author: TheBorzX
replies.body:
Thank you for the kind words and for taking the time to leave feedback! I'm really glad you enjoyed the gameplay. That was one of the main mechanics I wanted to make interesting and fun to experiment with.

Currently, the campaign consists of 6 handcrafted levels, with the first 3 available in the demo. I have plans to expand the game further in the future with new content and features.

Thanks again, and I hope you enjoy the remaining levels!

comments.author: Krakanu
comments.body:
Disclaimer: I only did the first 10 waves and finished the first level.  
  
Not being able to see enemies inside trees feels bad. At least have an outline or something. Also it wasn't clear to me that enemies could walk thru trees at first or if it slowed them down or something.

After the first level I got a 2/3 star rating. Not telling me the requirements for the stars ahead of time kinda sucks.

In later levels, add a checkpoint or two that enemies have to reach in addition to the end point, clever players can build the maze in a way to force enemies to backtrack thru parts of the maze multiple times.

Some of the art feels "too" detailed and just ends up looking busy and hard on the eyes. Especially when the game is not in full screen mode. Sometimes simple is better.

A neat trick I've heard to keep repeated sounds (like tower attacks) from being repetitive/grating on the ears is to slightly alter the pitch each time.

Since a ruin is worth 25 gold and replacing it with a wall is 5 gold, I don't see why you ever wouldn't clear them. Not sure what the goal is here.

Add a castle/fort or something at the end that clearly belongs to me. What am I even protecting?

replies.author: TheBorzX
replies.body:
Thanks! this is a genuinely useful list, and most of it is going into the next update.

Enemies moving through trees now show an outline so you can follow them, and the tutorial makes clear they pass straight through rather than being slowed. 

The three requirements are now shown up front, with a panel in the pause menu that tracks your progressduring the run. Repeated tower and death sounds now get a slight random pitch, which was a good tip.

The ruins,building a tower directly onto a ruin grants it extra range, and it's actually the only way to extend a tower's range in the game, so without that context clearing them understandably looked like the only move. There's a prompt for it now.

The checkpoint idea and adding a base at the exit are both ones I want to do, they're just larger pieces of work, so they'll come a little later. Thanks again for taking the time.

replies.author: Krakanu
replies.body:
I played a bit more. The guys that can break walls are annoying. Maybe less annoying if I could see charges above their head indicating how many walls they can break and let me see them recharging. Also I'm not sure if its intended that you can rebuild the wall right in front of them when they break it as it feels kind of cheesy.   
  
Idk how I would've finished the second stage without cheesing the last boss like that as they were still close to the end. I think it should take them 2 or 3 hits on the wall before they break it. Maybe add reinforced walls for 20 gold that can't be broken or take more hits to break.

replies.author: TheBorzX
replies.body:
I ended up making a few changes based on it.

The enemies now show their **Bash** charges above their heads, so it's much clearer how many walls they can still break. The Bulldozer has 2 Bash charges, while the Siege unit has 5.

I also changed how the Bulldozer works. Instead of instantly destroying a wall, it now has to bash it twice before breaking through and Siege boss needs to only charge once because he is the strongest boss. When they do, it leaves behind rubble that has to be cleared with gold before you can build on that tile again. My hope is that this makes wall-breaking feel more readable and tactical, while also making the choice between rebuilding and spending resources a bit more meaningful.

I'll keep an eye on the balance as more people play, but your feedback definitely helped shape these changes.

replies.author: promptling
replies.body: You’re already doing the part most AI demos skip: closing the feedback loop. The next useful test is handing this build to someone who hasn’t read the thread and seeing whether the enemy outline, star requirements, and ruin bonus now explain themselves. I’m building [Patchloop](https://patchloop.io/) to keep playtest findings tied to the exact build and subsequent patch. Linegrid Siege feels like a natural fit.
